html:
The Nimiipuu, "the people", better known by the French name Nez Perce, are a Sahaptian people of the Clearwater, Snake and Salmon river country where Idaho, Oregon and Washington meet. The map's Nez Perce territory shows the same people in later centuries.

They fished for salmon and dug camas roots, and after horses reached them in the early 1700s they became famous horse breeders; the spotted Appaloosa is linked with them. In 1805 they fed and guided the starving Lewis and Clark expedition. A treaty of 1855 left them a large reservation, but after gold was found a second treaty in 1863 cut it by about nine tenths. Bands that never signed it, led by Chief Joseph and others, fled toward Canada in the Nez Perce War of 1877 and surrendered in Montana after a retreat of some 1,900 kilometres. Their neighbours included the Cayuse and Umatilla.
